newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina confirms $2 bln bond issue to be 20-year.
newsitem.headline: Argentina confirms $2 bln bond issue to be 20-year.

text.p: Argentina's Economy Ministry confirmed Monday that its $2 billion global bond to be issued this week will have a 20-year maturity only.
The ministry added in a statement that it decided not to raise the amount issue as $2 billion will be enough to meet the Treasury's needs.
Argentina originally planned to issue a five-year tranche as well. Earlier Monday, joint lead manager J.P. Morgan said there would only be a 20-year maturity.
The bond was due to be launched on Tuesday, with pricing expected on Wednesday. Spread talk was around 475 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
The ministry added that 4.5 billion pesos in bonds are left to be issued by the end of 1997.
